chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Al-Fadl Abu al-Abbas from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
And complete the Hajj and the Umrah for Allah. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Both are obligatory.'

key_terms.حَجّ: Hajj, the major pilgrimage to Mecca
key_terms.عُمْرَة: Umrah, the minor pilgrimage to Mecca
key_terms.مَفْرُوضَانِ: Two obligatory duties (dual form of fard)

ai.seo_question: Are Hajj and Umrah both obligatory in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interprets the Quranic command to 'complete' Hajj and Umrah as establishing their obligatory status (fard), a key point in Shia jurisprudence regarding the completeness of these pillars. This clarification underscores that the ritual must be performed fully and exclusively for Allah's sake, distinguishing it from mere recommendation. The hadith serves as a foundational text linking the textual command of completion directly to legal obligation.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban Bin Usman, from Al Fazl Abu Al Abbas, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding [2:196] And complete the Hajj and the Umrah for Allah. Heasws said: ‘Both are necessities’.
en.sarwar: 2. AI-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated, from Mu‘afla’ ibn Muhammad, from al-Hassan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from al- Fadl abu af-‘Abbas who has said the following:
“About the words of Allah: ‘Complete al-Hajj and al-‘Umrah for the sake of Allah’ [2:196] abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that they are obligatory.”
